title: Change Detection & OnPush Strategy ⚡
description: Learn how Angular detects changes and how to dramatically improve performance with OnPush.

slides.title: How Angular Knows When to Update the UI 🔍
slides.content:
# Change Detection: The Engine Behind the View

Angular's change detection automatically keeps the model and the view in sync. By default, any event (click, HTTP response, timer) triggers a **full check** of all components from root to leaf.

* Angular maintains a tree of **change detectors**, one per component.
* Each detector compares the current state with the previous state and updates the DOM if necessary.
* This is fast for small apps, but can become a bottleneck in large applications.

quizData.question: By default, Angular's change detection runs only when you manually call detectChanges().
quizData.explanation: Change detection runs automatically in response to any asynchronous event (zone.js patches these).

slides.title: The Default Strategy (CheckAlways) 🔁
slides.content:
When any event occurs, Angular walks the entire component tree from top to bottom and checks every component’s bindings. This is called **CheckAlways**.

Even if a component’s inputs haven’t changed, its bindings are still re‑evaluated. For components deep in the tree, this wasted work adds up.

Angular provides an alternative: the **OnPush** strategy, which skips checks unless specific conditions are met.

slides.title: Enabling OnPush
slides.content: Set the change detection strategy in the component decorator:

quizData.question: With OnPush, when does Angular check a component?

options.text: Only when an @Input reference changes, an event inside the component occurs, or an async pipe emits.
Only when the component is first created.

quizData.explanation: OnPush marks the component for check only when an input changes (by reference), an event originates from the component, or an Observable pipe emits.

slides.title: Immutability & OnPush Go Hand in Hand 🤝
slides.content:
With OnPush, Angular checks @Input only if its **reference changes**. If you mutate an object or array (e.g., `this.items.push(newItem)`), the reference stays the same – no update.

**Always provide a new reference**:
```typescript
this.items = [...this.items, newItem];
```

This pairs perfectly with the store pattern from Chapter 10.

slides.title: Manually Triggering Change Detection
slides.content: In rare cases (e.g., after a third‑party library updates), inject `ChangeDetectorRef` and call `markForCheck()` or `detectChanges()`.

slides.title: Pro Tip 🚀
slides.content:
## Use OnPush Everywhere

For new components, make OnPush the default. It's a safe performance boost if you follow immutability. In the rare case you need CheckAlways, you can fall back.
